To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrodeposition of amorphus silicon thin films from organic electrolyte on Cu substrate using pulsed conditions has been studied for its application in lithium ion battery.

the electrodeposited silicon–oxygen–carbon thin films showed an increase in the capacity with a reduction in the first cycle irreversible capacity loss (FIR) and capacity fade with an increase in the pulse current frequency of electrodeposition.

the electrodeposition of Si thin films on Cu substrates from an organic ionic electrolytes using pulse current conditions can lead to a significant improvement in the electrochemical stability of these films and their electrochemical performance in a Li-ion battery configuration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrodeposition of silicon thin film anodes for lithium ion batteries.
the development of silicon anodes for high-performance lithium ion batteries.
the electrodeposition of silicon thin films on copper substrates from organic ionic liquid electrolytes using pulsed current deposition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pulsed current electrodeposition of silicon thin films on the Cu substrate from an organic electrolyte can be a promising approach to improve the stability of these films.

the pulse electrodeposition of Si thin films at a higher frequency (5000 Hz) results in a better electrochemical performance compared to the electrodeposition of Si at lower frequency (500 Hz) due to a better structural stability of these films.
the pulse electrodeposits Si thin films with better structural and morphological properties and hence better electrochemical properties compared to the DC deposited films
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pulse current electrodeposition of silicon thin films is an attractive method to produce stable silicon thin films for lithium ion battery applications.
the electrodeposition of silicon anodes using organic ionic liquid electrolyte is a promising route to produce silicon thin films with good performance for Li ion battery applications.

the pulse current electrodeposition of silicon thin films on copper substrates using a room temperature organic ionic electrolytes can produce stable and high capacity silicon thin films with good cycling stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the electrodeposition of silicon anodes using organic ionic electrolytes and pulse electrodeposition conditions can be used to improve the performance of silicon thin film anodes for lithium ion batteries.
pulsed current electrodeposition can provide a new avenue for the deposition of Si thin films with improved stability.

the pulse current electrodeposition conditions can be used as a simple and cost-effective technique to improve the electrochemical performance of silicon thin films for lithium ion battery applications.
